text:
alex: Thinking out loud — proposal to move from a hard on-demand floor to a "soft-floor" model for our mixed pools. goal: preserve p95 latency SLO while getting more spot % during off-peak.

maria: Love it. Can you sketch the operational difference? i.e. when does soft-floor pull from on-demand vs spot fallback?

alex: Sketch: keep persistent on-demand for the core baseline (70% of baseline qps by default). remaining demand -> spot burst pool. if spot interruption or drain predicted, we use interruption credits + short-lived on-demand top-ups for ~2-3 minutes while we drain/evict. If extended pressure, trigger model-fallback (smaller model) + degrade features.

sam: curious on numbers — 70% is pretty specific. why that vs 50/80?

alex: picked 70% from sims that balance cost and tail-latency. quick calc: current baseline on-demand 1.0x cost, spot is ~0.35x. if we move 30% of baseline traffic to spot burst we save ~ 20% total infra cost on average, with a <2% increase in throttles without mitigation. can tune per-region.

ria: we should also bake in a regional safety multiplier. us-east1 has much lower spot reliability than us-west2 sometimes.

nina: +1. ops question: how do we account for network hot-spots? some racks hit NIC saturations when bursting.

alex: good call. part of the config will set 'burst_bandwidth_limit' per AZ and a concurrency cap per spot instance type. i can add heuristics to detect NIC saturation and lower burst concurrency.

tj: what metrics do we need to monitor for the experiment? and what's the rollback criteria?

maria: from product/infra side: p50/p95 generation latency, request failures (5xx/504), queue length, #interruption events, on-demand top-up ops, cost delta. rollback if p95 increases > 20% or errors +2% sustained for 10m.

sam: add 'feature-availability' tags so we can correlate degraded UX (like stop-streaming) with infra events.

alex: here's a rough config we can deploy to the staging pool for the canary:

```
pool_config:
  mode: mixed
  base_on_demand_fraction: 0.7
  burst_pool: spot
  interruption_credit_seconds: 120
  topup_policy:
    immediate_on_interrupt: true
    max_topup_duration_sec: 300
  burst_bandwidth_limit_mbps: 300
  per_instance_concurrency_cap: 8
  model_fallback_sequence: [redwood-7b-quant, redwood-3b-quant]
```

alex: also adding tracing tags: burst_reason, topup_trigger, interruption_id

ria: ops runbook snippet for spot drain?

nina: i'll paste a short runbook that devops-bot can trigger on drain detection.

devops-bot: @channel detected spot-drain in us-west2-a (estimate 60s). starting top-up workflow, tag trace=2113456789-canary

nina: runbook (abbrev):
1) detect drain (provider signal OR > 3 interruptions in 60s)
2) scale on-demand by +x containers (x = min(ceil(current_spot_instances/4), 10))
3) add interruption tag to requests and enable idempotent retry window = 120s
4) if on-demand capacity not available within 180s -> trigger model-fallback and route new sessions to degraded route
5) alert infra-oncall if failover > 180s

maria: good. also add an automated cost guard: if topups drive hourly cost > +30% vs baseline, pause canary and notify finance+pm.

sam: what about long-running batches that don't like interruption credits? recommend marking batch lanes as "non-burst" and keep them on-demand always.

alex: yes — lane-level tags. batch_lane: pinned_on_demand = true

ria: can we do a small A/B? 10% traffic soft-floor, 40% hard-floor (current), 50% control? run for 2 weeks and compare tail-latency and cost.

alex: plan: canary in us-west2 with the 10% soft-floor, instrument everything. run 48h smoke, then 2 weeks full sample if smoke passes. will push a feature flag to rollout.

nina: we should also expose interruption reasons in the console dashboard for quick triage (preemptible, maintenance, capacity reclaim).

tj: who owns the alert thresholds and SLO changes? need a small ownership doc.

alex: i can own the canary and instrumentation. ria take the region config heuristics. marta (cc: not in thread) will own cost guard hook. ops-oncall will need to review runbook.

maria: next steps: alex open PR with pool_config + telemetry + runbook. tia (QA) will run failure injection sim: simulate 2-minute continuous interruptions and 5-minute prolonged drain.

sam: also add a small chaos test that simulates NIC saturation + burst traffic to validate concurrency cap.

alex: ok i'll do the PR today. tagging time estimates: PR + unit tests 1d, deploy to staging 1d, canary 2w if green. will post rollout plan and dashboard links in this thread.

ria: thanks. if we hit >25% cost drop and <5% UX regressions we should consider rolling to more regions.

alex: noted. starting PR now.

devops-bot: action_logged: alex opened PR #4958 for soft-floor canary (link hidden)

alex: thanks all. will update here with smoke results.
